rv.q: Again, Khan and Salinsky have made yesterday’s news a headline event.
With its strong writing, fine performances, and excellent direction from Josh Roche, In the Print is very accessible even for those not familiar with the political situation of the 1980s.

Director Josh Roche brings a claustrophobic air to events as Jolly’s spiky, hard-nosed Dean (the actor’s extraordinary similarity to Angela Rayner may or may not be casting happenstance) faces up to the “malevolent cane toad” that is Murdoch.
This important play reminds us of what always happens when new technology created by workers reduces the labour time they need to deliver.
For anyone with an interest in the period and how it changed the media, this show has a lot of fascinating drama rooted in recent history.

Unfortunately the wit and erudition which added such a light touch to proceedings in The Gang of Three (as Jenkins, Healey and Crosland vied over G&Ts for the Labour Party leadership in the 1970s and beyond), are lacking in the dialogue here.
So this sharp, well-researched new play of conversations and confrontations is gripping.

cn.t: A well-crafted docudrama distills the 1986 Wapping dispute into a compelling interpersonal battle between Brenda Dean and Rupert Murdoch, though some find it lacks the charm and subtlety of the writers' previous work.
